findings.explanation: HOL4 defines locnrow only on POSN. The Definition is made by Prim_rec.new_recursive_definition through new_specification (Prim_rec.sml:259-285), so the only saved fact is locnrow (POSN r c) = r. The values at UNKNOWNpt and EOFpt are independent and open. Lean sends both to the same ARB, so it proves locnrow UNKNOWNpt = locnrow EOFpt, and also that both equal locncol UNKNOWNpt. HOL4 proves neither.
findings.repair:
opaque locnrow_spec : {f : locn → Nat // ∀ r c, f (.POSN r c) = r} :=
  ⟨fun | .POSN r _ => r | _ => 0, fun _ _ => rfl⟩

def locnrow : locn → Nat := locnrow_spec.1

theorem locnrow_def (r c : Nat) : locnrow (.POSN r c) = r := locnrow_spec.2 r c
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.Location

example : locnrow locn.UNKNOWNpt = locnrow locn.EOFpt := by simp [locnrow]
findings.hol4_check: ?f:locn->num. (!r c. f (POSN r c) = r) /\ f UNKNOWNpt <> f EOFpt

findings.explanation: HOL4 specifies locn_rowupdate f only on POSN (new_specification, sole fact locn_rowupdate f (POSN r c) = POSN (f r) c). Its values at UNKNOWNpt and EOFpt are open and may depend on the constructor and on f. Lean returns one ARB for every f and both constructors, so it proves locn_rowupdate f UNKNOWNpt = locn_rowupdate g EOFpt, and equality with locn_colupdate there. HOL4 leaves these open.
findings.repair:
opaque locn_rowupdate_spec :
    {u : (Nat → Nat) → locn → locn // ∀ f r c, u f (.POSN r c) = .POSN (f r) c} :=
  ⟨fun f l => match l with | .POSN r c => .POSN (f r) c | l => l, fun _ _ _ => rfl⟩

def locn_rowupdate : (Nat → Nat) → locn → locn := locn_rowupdate_spec.1

theorem locn_rowupdate_def (f : Nat → Nat) (r c : Nat) :
    locn_rowupdate f (.POSN r c) = .POSN (f r) c := locn_rowupdate_spec.2 f r c
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.Location

example (f g : Nat → Nat) : locn_rowupdate f locn.UNKNOWNpt = locn_rowupdate g locn.EOFpt := by simp [locn_rowupdate]
findings.hol4_check: ?u:(num->num)->locn->locn. (!f r c. u f (POSN r c) = POSN (f r) c) /\ !f. u f UNKNOWNpt <> u f EOFpt

findings.explanation: HOL4 specifies locncol only on POSN (new_specification, sole fact locncol (POSN r c) = c). The values at UNKNOWNpt and EOFpt are independent and open. Lean maps both to the same ARB, so it proves locncol UNKNOWNpt = locncol EOFpt, and also locncol UNKNOWNpt = locnrow UNKNOWNpt. HOL4's saved theorems do not decide these.
findings.repair:
opaque locncol_spec : {f : locn → Nat // ∀ r c, f (.POSN r c) = c} :=
  ⟨fun | .POSN _ c => c | _ => 0, fun _ _ => rfl⟩

def locncol : locn → Nat := locncol_spec.1

theorem locncol_def (r c : Nat) : locncol (.POSN r c) = c := locncol_spec.2 r c
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.Location

example : locncol locn.UNKNOWNpt = locncol locn.EOFpt := by simp [locncol]
findings.hol4_check: ?f:locn->num. (!r c. f (POSN r c) = c) /\ f UNKNOWNpt <> f EOFpt

findings.explanation: HOL4 specifies locn_colupdate f only on POSN (new_specification, sole fact locn_colupdate f (POSN r c) = POSN r (f c)). Its values at UNKNOWNpt and EOFpt are open and may depend on the constructor and on f. Lean returns one ARB for every f and both constructors, so it proves locn_colupdate f UNKNOWNpt = locn_colupdate g EOFpt. HOL4 leaves this open.
findings.repair:
opaque locn_colupdate_spec :
    {u : (Nat → Nat) → locn → locn // ∀ f r c, u f (.POSN r c) = .POSN r (f c)} :=
  ⟨fun f l => match l with | .POSN r c => .POSN r (f c) | l => l, fun _ _ _ => rfl⟩

def locn_colupdate : (Nat → Nat) → locn → locn := locn_colupdate_spec.1

theorem locn_colupdate_def (f : Nat → Nat) (r c : Nat) :
    locn_colupdate f (.POSN r c) = .POSN r (f c) := locn_colupdate_spec.2 f r c
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.Location

example (f g : Nat → Nat) : locn_colupdate f locn.UNKNOWNpt = locn_colupdate g locn.EOFpt := by simp [locn_colupdate]
findings.hol4_check: ?u:(num->num)->locn->locn. (!f r c. u f (POSN r c) = POSN r (f c)) /\ !f. u f UNKNOWNpt <> u f EOFpt
